newsitem.title: UK: JLP's Waitrose supermarkets report strong 1996.
newsitem.headline: JLP's Waitrose supermarkets report strong 1996.

text.p: Britain's Waitrose supermarket chain, owned by the John Lewis Partnership , reported a hefty 11 percent rise in gross sales for 1996 on Thursday and said it had consolidated its position in the competitive British food retail market.

JLP, which operates 115 Waitrose branches as well as 23 department stores, reported record profits of 217 million pounds ($350 million) prior to its profit share among employees, and a 45 percent rise in profit after this distribution to 135.3 million pounds.

The company said in a statement that it was confident about the current year but added that the competitive climate was tough and "we cannot help but be hit by ricochets from the crossfire between the most aggressive players on the field."
JLP, which works on a co-operative partnership basis, said department store sales jumped 13 percent with no new store openings during the year.
